blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse applied to Capital Markets & Wealth Management. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Wealth and capital-markets clients buy judgment and pay for experience: advisors need research and portfolio context in minutes, operations need settlement and reconciliation without firefights, and compliance needs evidence without expeditions.

items: Positions, performance and fees reconcile from extracts; client questions wait on report runs.
Advisors assemble portfolio context from terminals, PDFs and CRM; response quality depends on prep time.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Banking & Financial Services level this capability reads as: credit, market, liquidity and ops risk on one governed estate with BCBS 239-style lineage (report lineage questions answered in hours). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
